label: Distance to target
summary: Whether the distance between this place and a target place, measured in map pixels and squared, passes a comparison.
details: The game compares the squared distance because it is cheaper to compute than the real one. So the number you compare with must be a squared value too. Vanilla compares against named values such as squared_distance_medium and squared_distance_large. It works on a title (county, barony) or a province.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The place to measure the distance to.
fields.values: a province, barony or county, e.g. root.capital_province

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison on the squared distance.
fields.values: a comparison with a number or a named value, e.g. <= squared_distance_medium

label: Starting gold by income
summary: Whether the starting gold the game calculates for the character from their income passes a comparison.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla does not use it. It is probably meant for setting up a character's starting gold, but that is a guess from the name.

label: Matches group
summary: Whether the character falls into a fixed, repeatable share of all characters picked for a named group.
details: The match is a number from 0.0 to 1.0. With 0.1, about 10% of all characters pass, and it is always the same characters for the same group name. Nothing is random beyond the group's name, so it is a stable way to split characters into subsets. Instead of a group name you can give a scope, and its value is used as the group name.

fields.name: group
fields.text: A name that identifies the group. Different names give different subsets.
fields.values: any name you choose, e.g. dog_ear_type

fields.name: scope
fields.text: Used instead of group: a scope whose value serves as the group name.

fields.name: match
fields.text: The share of characters that pass, 0.0 (none) to 1.0 (all).

label: Stewardship skill
summary: Whether the character's stewardship skill passes a comparison.
details: Vanilla mostly compares it with named skill ratings such as high_skill_rating or decent_skill_rating.

label: Stewardship difference
summary: Whether the difference between the character's stewardship skill and another character's passes a comparison.
details: The game's documentation does not say which skill is subtracted from which. Vanilla's one use (target = scope:vizier, value >= -5) suggests it is the character's skill minus the target's, so a negative result would mean the target is better; that is an inference. With abs = yes the sign is ignored, so only the size of the difference counts. Left out, abs is no.

fields.name: value
fields.values: a comparison with a number or script value, e.g. >= -5

fields.name: abs
fields.text: Whether the sign of the difference is ignored.

label: Stewardship for portrait
summary: Whether the character's stewardship skill, scaled to a range from 0.0 to 1.0, passes a comparison.
details: The game's documentation says the scaling is meant for portraits. Vanilla's scripts do not use it.

label: Stewardship perk points
summary: Whether the number of perk points the character has available passes a comparison.
details: The game's documentation does not name the lifestyle; that it is the stewardship one comes from the key name. Vanilla uses it once, comparing with the named value max_perk_amount_per_lifestyle.

label: Stewardship perks owned
summary: Whether the number of perks the character has from the stewardship lifestyle passes a comparison.

label: Unlockable stewardship perks
summary: Whether the number of stewardship perks the character could unlock right now passes a comparison.
details: A perk counts when the character already has the perks it depends on and its own conditions (can_be_picked) are met. Perk points are not checked, so a character with none can still count perks.

label: Stewardship lifestyle XP
summary: Whether a count tied to the character's stewardship lifestyle passes a comparison; the game's documentation text is unclear what it counts.
details: The game's documentation text repeats the sentence of the perk points trigger ("how many perk points available"), which looks like a copy mistake. Reading it as the experience gathered in the lifestyle comes from the name only.

label: Kind of story
summary: Whether the story in scope is of the given story type.
details: Vanilla checks for types such as story_cycle_pet_dog, story_cycle_hunt_mystical_animal or story_greatest_of_khans.

label: Stress
summary: Whether the character's stress amount passes a comparison.
details: Vanilla often checks for any stress (> 0), for plain numbers such as >= 50, or for named values such as high_stress and normal_baseline_stress. For the stress level use stress_level.

label: Stress level
summary: Whether the character's stress level passes a comparison.
details: Vanilla compares it with small whole numbers (1, 2 and 3), for example >= 2. For the stress amount use stress instead.

label: Strife opinion
summary: Whether the strife opinion value the character has accumulated passes a comparison.
details: Vanilla uses it three times, always as >= 1. The game does not explain what strife opinion is beyond that.

label: Sub-realm size
summary: Whether the number of counties in the character's sub-realm passes a comparison.
details: Vanilla compares with plain numbers such as >= 10 or named sizes such as medium_realm_size.

label: Current phase
summary: Whether a situation's sub-region is currently in the given phase.
details: Vanilla uses it with the seasons of the steppe situation, for example situation_steppe_cold_zud_season, and with phases such as phase_exceptional_bounty. It works on a sub-region of a situation.

label: Days in current phase
summary: Whether the number of days since the sub-region's current situation phase began passes a comparison.

label: Days until phase ends
summary: Whether the number of days left until the sub-region's current situation phase ends passes a comparison.

label: Phase end date
summary: Whether the date on which the sub-region's current situation phase ends passes a comparison.
details: The right side must be a valid date.

label: Phase start date
summary: Whether the date on which the sub-region's current situation phase started passes a comparison.
details: The right side must be a valid date.

label: Can break tributary
summary: Whether the character can break out of the tributary relationship they are currently a subject in.
details: A tributary is a ruler who pays a more powerful ruler (the suzerain). Write yes or no. Vanilla uses it four times, all with yes.

label: Contract has flag
summary: Whether any currently active obligation in the character's subject contract carries the given flag.
details: The subject contract is the character's contract as a subject (for example a vassal or tributary). Vanilla checks flags such as vassal_contract_liege_forced_war_override and tributary_contract_suzerain_guarantee_override.

label: Contract can be modified
summary: Whether the character has a subject contract that can be changed at all.
details: It needs three things: the character has a contract, the contract uses obligation levels, and the character is a count or higher. Write yes or no.

label: Contract blocked from changes
summary: Whether script has blocked the character's subject contract from being modified.
details: The block is set with the effect set_subject_contract_modification_blocked. Write yes or no.

label: Obligation level can go down
summary: Whether the obligation level of a named obligation in the character's subject contract can be lowered.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla does not use it. How the contract is named is not shown in the input.

label: Obligation level can go up
summary: Whether the obligation level of a named obligation in the character's subject contract can be raised.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla does not use it. How the contract is named is not shown in the input.

label: Subject standing
summary: Whether the standing the character's subject contract has built up passes a comparison.
details: It can be negative; vanilla also checks < 0. Vanilla uses plain numbers (> 20) and named values such as seal_of_investiture_minimum_subject_standing.

label: Appointment investment
summary: Whether the amount the scoped character has invested in a title, towards a given candidate, passes a comparison.
details: Vanilla always compares it with scope:actor.appointment_investment_cap (value < ...), which looks like a check that there is still room to invest; that is an inference from the name of the cap.

fields.name: title
fields.text: The title the investment is made in.

fields.name: candidate
fields.text: The candidate the investment goes towards.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison on the invested amount.

label: Switch
summary: Picks one list of triggers to check, depending on what another trigger gives.
details: You name one trigger. Each case is a possible value of it with the triggers to test when it matches. An optional fallback runs when no case matches. Vanilla uses it with triggers like has_game_rule and scheme_skill, with rule values or skill names as cases.

fields.name: trigger
fields.text: The trigger whose value decides which case is used.
fields.values: a trigger that takes a single value

fields.name: <case>
fields.text: A possible value of that trigger, with the triggers to check when it matches.

fields.name: fallback
fields.text: The triggers to check when no case matches.

label: Is de facto liege or above
summary: Whether the given title is the scoped title's de facto liege title, or one above it.
details: De facto means by who actually holds the titles now, not by the map's borders. Write the title to check against. Vanilla mostly uses the holder's primary title, such as root.primary_title.

label: Is de jure liege or above
summary: Whether the given title is the scoped title's de jure liege title, or one above it.
details: De jure means by the map's own borders (which kingdom a duchy belongs to), whoever holds them. Write the title to check against, such as scope:title or title:h_china.

label: Is liege or above
summary: Whether the given character is the scoped character's liege, or stands above them in the chain of lieges.
details: Write the character to check, such as scope:actor. Vanilla uses it a lot.

label: Is same or above
summary: Whether the given character is the scoped character themselves, or stands above them in the vassal hierarchy.
details: It reads like target_is_liege_or_above, but is also true when the given character is the scoped character.

label: Is vassal or below
summary: Whether the given character is a vassal of the scoped character, or lower in their vassal hierarchy.
details: A character who is not a ruler does not count as a vassal. Write the character to check, such as scope:recipient.

label: Target weight
summary: Whether the character's target weight passes a comparison.
details: The game's documentation gives only the example target_weight > 10. Vanilla does not use it, and the input does not say what the weight is.

label: Contract tier
summary: Whether the task contract's tier passes a comparison.
details: Vanilla compares it with the defined tiers (define:NTaskContract|HIGH_TASK_CONTRACT_TIER and the medium and low ones) or with values like task_contract_t3_value. It runs on a task contract.

label: Tax collector aptitude
summary: Whether the character's aptitude as a tax collector in a given kind of tax slot passes a comparison.
details: The aptitude ranges from 0 to 4. Vanilla only uses the clan tax slot.

fields.name: target
fields.values: a tax slot type, e.g. clan_tax_slot

label: Tax to liege
summary: Whether the amount of tax the character sends to their liege passes a comparison.

label: Tenet sees trait as sin
summary: Whether the given trait counts as a sin under the tenet in scope.
details: A tenet is a belief of a faith. Write the trait, for example gluttonous. Vanilla uses it once, with prev.

label: Tenet sees trait as virtue
summary: Whether the given trait counts as a virtue under the tenet in scope.
details: A tenet is a belief of a faith. Write the trait, for example chaste. Vanilla mostly checks lustful.
